To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the S-layer of C. glutamicium is highly variable in its primary structure and that this structural variability is reflected by the surface layer architecture of the cells.

the S-layer of C. glutamicium is composed of five phylogenetically distinct classes of S-layer proteins, and that the sequence similarity-based S-layer protein classification is reflected by a class-specific S-layer morphology.

the S-layer protein of Corynebacteriurn glutamicum exhibits a mosaic structure, that the mosaic structure can be classified into five different classes, that the S-layer structure is hexagonal and that there is a correlation between the primary structure of S-layer proteins and the S-layer morphology.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the classification of the C. glutamicum S-layer proteins, which are the first characterized S-layer proteins of Gram-positive, low-G+C-content bacteria.
the characterization of the C. glutamicum S-layer proteins by sequence and structure analysis.
the classification of S-layer proteins of C. glutamicus by sequence analyses and by atomic force microscopy, which is the first report about the S-layer structure of this species.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the S-layers of C. glutamicium are highly variable and show a mosaic structure of conserved and variable regions.
the primary structure of S-layer proteins is a major determinant for their morphology and that sequence analyses are a valuable tool to predict the morphology of S-layers.
the C. glutaticum S-layers are composed of a highly conserved and a highly variable domain, and this is a common feature of all S-layer proteins.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the S-layer of Corynebacterin glutamicum is a very flexible protein with respect to its amino acid sequence, which is reflected in the morphological diversity of the protein layer.
C. glutamicium S-layer proteins are highly conserved in their primary structure, whereas the surface morphology of C. glutamicim S-layers is highly variable.
the C. glutumaticum S-layer proteins are a group of structurally related proteins that exhibit significant sequence diversity, which is reflected by differences in the S-layer structure.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the S-layer of the C. glutamicum is a highly conserved structure that can be divided into five phylogenetically different classes, and the S-layer proteins exhibit a mosaic structure.
S-layer proteins are a very useful target for the classification of Corynebacteriales.
